chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Even if you think, or it reaches you, that this matter will occur tomorrow, do not abandon seeking livelihood; and if you are able to not be a burden [on others], then do so.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The matter/affair — in Shia tradition, a coded reference to the Rising (Qiyam) of al-Qa'im, the awaited Imam who will establish justice
key_terms.طَلَبُ الرِّزْقِ: Seeking sustenance/livelihood — the act of earning one's keep through lawful work
key_terms.كَلًّا: A burden — one who is dependent on others for sustenance, unable to support himself

ai.seo_question: Should Muslims continue working and seeking livelihood while waiting for the return of al-Mahdi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised his companion Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi that even in the expectation of the imminent Rising of al-Qa'im (the eschatological redeemer), one must not abandon earning a livelihood. The phrase 'this matter' (هَذَا الْأَمْرَ) was understood by the early Shia community as a reference to the appearance of the Qa'im from the family of the Prophet. The teaching balances eschatological hope with pragmatic responsibility: believers should maintain their economic self-sufficiency and not become dependent on others, even when anticipating transformative events.
